newsitem.title: USA: Hector gets waiver for Nasdaq trading.
newsitem.headline: Hector gets waiver for Nasdaq trading.

text.p: Hector Communications Corp said Monday it was granted a waiver from the tangible net worth requirements of the Nasdaq Stock Market, which will enable the company to continue trading on the Nasdaq National Market.
The company said following its acquisition last April of Minnesota-based Ollig Utilities Co it had negative tangible net worth, which normally precludes a company from trading on Nasdaq.
Earlier, the operator of independent telephone companies and cable television systems reported third quarter earnings of $0.13 per share, up from $0.05 a year ago.

Chairman Curtis Sampson said the third quarter marked the first full three-month contribution of Alliance Communications, a jointly-owned venture in which Hector holds a 68 percent equity interest, to the company's consolidated operating results.

Sampson said the Ollig transaction is continuing to work as planned by generating substantially higher operating revenues, profitability and cash flows. He added that due to the positive fourth quarter outlook, 1996 shapes up to be one of Hector's strongest years in its history.
